newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Norilsk strike plan early but earnest - union leader.
newsitem.headline: Norilsk strike plan early but earnest - union leader.

text.p: Workers at the flagship plant of Russia's Norilsk Nickel are seriously considering the possibility of striking March 15, but the proposal is in draft form and needs full approval, a union official said Wednesday.
Boris Degtyaryov, deputy head of the plant's United Trade Union committee, told Reuters from the Arctic town of Norilsk that workers' patience on overdue salaries had run out.

"I understand that no matter how strong someone's patience is, when he has not been paid for such a long time, it has its limits," Degtyaryov said. "From this point of view, we can say that a strike is a real possibility."
He said the strike proposal in its current form envisaged disrupting output "for an indefinite period of time".
"The organising board (of the United Trade Union committee) said that any strike would involve workers engaged in basic output at the plant," he said.
Degtyaryov said the decision to write a draft strike proposal was taken earlier on Wednesday by the United Trade Union committee's organising board.
A vote on the draft proposal would take place on March 1, the date set for a meeting between labour representatives and Norilsk Nickel management.
Degtyaryov said that if the committee formally approved the draft, there would be a further five days for both sides to try to settle the dispute.
If the talks failed to break the deadlock, another 10 days would elapse before workers actually laid down their tools, Degtyaryov said.
"This explains the (strike) date set for March 15," he said.
He said the committee would write to Norilsk management before launching any strike.
Degtyaryov said Norilsk salary and holiday arrears totalled 900 billion roubles ($160 million).
Workers are also demanding wages be boosted by what a RAO Norilsky Nickel spokesman said earlier would cost the company 70 billion roubles ($12.4 million) a month.

RAO spokesmen had said earlier this month that wage arrears were about 1.3 trillion roubles, but the amount has been brought down to 900 billion roubles over an unspecified time, company officials said.

RAO Norilsk Nickel is a major supplier of nickel, cobalt, and platinum group metals to world markets. Last year the main metals plant produced around 100,000 tonnes of nickel from the group's total nickel output of 177,185 tonnes.
